title: The improvement policy in force runs the organization's own improvement work
labels: DETERMINISTIC FIXTURE PROVIDER — scripted workers in real processes; no model was run
SYNTHETIC DATA — every request, team, dataset and value is invented
SYNTHETIC — the review workload, the 30 unverified complaints and the library of candidate fixes (some deliberately flawed)
One campaign per policy: a case study, not a statistical comparison

steps.claim: The organization keeps a portfolio of hypotheses built from its own recorded observations
steps.observed: 13 verified review failures in 5 classes, plus 30 unverified reports of one complaint; 8 hypotheses

steps.claim: The policy of the release in force decides each step, inside a bounded budget
steps.observed: r1's policy (frequency-first) took 8 decisions and used 712 of 900 units

steps.claim: The replacement policy first has to pass the release gate
steps.observed: accept: Accepted: validated_benefit improved by 12.6167 against the incumbent (95% interval 0.4167 to 25.4333) with every hard gate passed.

steps.claim: During the canary the new policy decides, and the default has not changed
steps.observed: 7 decisions under canary can_0mwgxuthc1paa2e14aa; active release still r1

steps.claim: Replacing the policy changes what the organization works on
steps.observed: frequency-first began with style_strict; expected-value began with guard_removed_toplevel and piloted 2 times before submitting

steps.claim: Every submission from either policy was decided by the same release gate
steps.observed: control: 1 accepted, style_strict (inconclusive) not accepted; trial: 1 accepted, guard_type_strict (rejected) not accepted

steps.claim: Each approach that did not pass is recorded so it is not repeated blindly
steps.observed: [suspected] Adding the style_strict check to change review (built on r1) was inconclusive at the release gate: No demonstr… | [verified] Adding the guard_type_strict check to change review (built on r1) was rejected at the release gate: Rejected: …

steps.claim: The canary is observed, then retained
steps.observed: actions the runtime had to refuse: 0; r2 is now the default for future work

steps.claim: A fix qualified against the old default is not promoted over the new one
steps.observed: Release r3 was qualified against r1, but r2 is now active. Rebuild the candidate on r2 and evaluate it again. All 8 hypotheses were reopened to be rebuilt on r2.
